title: Playbook execution cost scorer and safety gates
author: Asha Patel
description:
Context: On-call teams maintain many playbooks; some are expensive to execute (multiple API calls, large artifact fetches, or cross-service writes). We need tooling to estimate the operational cost of running a playbook and to guard automatic or semi-automatic runners from executing high-cost operations without explicit approval. This PR introduces a playbook execution cost scorer (heuristic + lightweight model) and a configurable safety-gates layer that prevents automatic remediation or scheduled runs when estimated cost or blast radius exceeds team thresholds.

What this PR does (high level): Adds a cost scoring pipeline that inspects playbook steps and produces a cost_estimate (tokens: estimate of API/compute units, external_io: bytes, blast_score: heuristic for domain impact). Integrates the score into the playbook preview UI/CLI and the runbook-executor path. Adds safety gate checks with three enforcement modes: warn, require-ack, block. Adds telemetry (playbook.cost_estimate.histogram, playbook.safety_gate.blocked_count) and a small data-driven configuration for cost weightings stored in internal/cost_model.json. Ships docs and a CLI preview flag (--preview-cost) so oncall can get an approximate cost before running.

Motivation: Reduce surprise operational spend, avoid automated remediation that causes large downstream effects, and give SREs a lightweight signal to prioritize lightweight vs heavy playbooks. This is intended to be conservative (overestimate rather than undercount) and extensible to more accurate models later.

Checklist:
- [x] cost scorer core implementation (pkg/playbook/scorer.go)
- [x] safety gate enforcement and modes (pkg/playbook/safety_gates.go)
- [x] CLI preview and UI integration (cmd/ptool, docs)
- [x] unit + integration tests (tests/playbook/*)
- [x] telemetry + dashboard notes (docs/observability.md)
- [x] defaults and config schema (internal/cost_model.json, charts values)
- [x] migration note for teams that rely on automatic-approved runs

Backward compatibility: New fields are additive (playbook metadata now includes cost_estimate). Default enforcement mode is "warn" so behavior is opt-in. No breaking changes expected for existing playbooks.

Risk & mitigations: The scorer is intentionally conservative; misestimates could be noisy. We ship with a metrics dashboard to monitor false positives and tune internal/cost_model.json. Safety gate config default prevents accidental blocking.

Related: ENG-1289 (playbook hygiene), SRE-342 (remediation safety posture).

review_comments: Liam O'Connor: Nice incremental approach. Please add a short comment on why the default weights overestimate (we should be explicit). Also add unit tests for a playbook with mixed IO + compute steps.
Author (Asha Patel): Added tests for blended playbooks and documented conservative defaults in internal/cost_model.json (see commit d12ef7b).
Priya Rao: For safety_gates, ensure configuration can be overridden per-team via the helm values file. Can we also expose an opt-out annotation on playbooks?
Author: Added support for playbook.annotations['slo-toolkit/safety-gate'] = 'off' and document it. Helm values updated to allow per-namespace defaults.
Mateo Silva: CI flaked on the integration test once (network timeout). Re-ran and everything passed. Suggest we add a short note about expected variance in metrics for the first week after rollout.
Liam O'Connor (approve): Tests look solid and UX is reasonable. Approving with a request to monitor telemetry for tuning in the first release window.
release_notes: Adds a conservative playbook execution cost estimator and configurable safety-gates to prevent automatic or scheduled playbook runs above team-defined cost/blast thresholds. Includes CLI preview (--preview-cost), telemetry, docs, and a migration note. Default enforcement mode is 'warn'.
additional_notes: Follow-up work planned: (1) add a lighter-weight approximate model for offline scoring of hundreds of archived playbooks (ENG-1350), (2) add a per-team dashboard to tune cost weights, (3) prototype ML-based cost estimator using historical run data.
